Feature build in /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router + Prisma + Postgres). Add **secure image attachments to the live chat** (customer widget + admin inbox): users can paste an image from clipboard OR click a paperclip to attach a file. Security is critical. You OWN prisma/schema.prisma this round (other work is not touching it). Do NOT run git. Do NOT run `prisma db push` against any database (the parent will deploy migrations). You MAY run `npx prisma generate` and `npx prisma validate`.

Read first: components/ChatWidget.tsx, components/admin/ChatInbox.tsx, lib/actions-chat.ts, app/api/chat/route.ts and app/api/chat/[id]/route.ts, and the ChatConversation/ChatMessage models in prisma/schema.prisma. Match existing style and auth patterns.

Requirements:
1. **Schema**: add image storage. Add a `ChatAttachment` model: `id`, `messageId` (relation to ChatMessage, or make ChatMessage optionally carry one attachment — pick the cleaner fit), `mime` String, `sizeBytes` Int, `data` Bytes (store the image bytes in Postgres — avoids filesystem/permission issues; the web runs as a non-root user that can only write .next). Add the relation to ChatMessage. Run `npx prisma generate` after.
2. **Upload (server)**: add a server action or extend the chat API to accept an image with a message. Enforce ALL of these — this is the security core:
   - Allowed MIME: ONLY `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`. REJECT everything else. **Explicitly reject `image/svg+xml`** (SVG enables XSS).
   - Validate the real bytes, not just the client-declared type: check magic-number/file signature (PNG `89 50 4E 47`, JPEG `FF D8 FF`, GIF `47 49 46 38`, WEBP `RIFF....WEBP`). Reject on mismatch.
   - Max size 5 MB. Reject larger.
   - Authorization: only the conversation's participant (the customer who owns/started it, matched by userId or the anon session/conversation token the widget already uses) or an ADMIN may attach to a conversation. Reuse the existing chat auth model — read how route.ts / actions-chat.ts authorize today and mirror it exactly.
   - Rate-limit uploads (reuse lib/rate-limit checkRateLimit if present).
3. **Serve (server)**: add an authorized route e.g. `app/api/chat/attachment/[id]/route.ts` that streams the bytes ONLY to an authorized viewer (participant or admin — same check as upload). Set headers: correct `Content-Type` (from stored mime), `Content-Disposition: inline; filename="image"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and a restrictive `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'`. Never serve as text/html. No path traversal (id is a DB id, not a filename).
4. **Customer widget (components/ChatWidget.tsx)**: add a paperclip icon button (hidden file input, `accept="image/png,image/jpeg,image/gif,image/webp"`) AND an `onPaste` handler on the input that reads image blobs from the clipboard. Show a small thumbnail preview before send; allow removing it. On send, upload the image and render sent/received image messages as thumbnails (clicking opens full size). Client-side: also validate type+size before upload (fast feedback), but never rely on client validation for security.
5. **Admin inbox (components/admin/ChatInbox.tsx)**: render image messages as thumbnails that open full-size; admins can also attach images in their replies the same way.

Verify: `cd /opt/nxeon && npx prisma generate` succeeds, `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` is clean for your files, and `npm run build` exits 0. Report the files changed, the exact security controls enforced, and confirm SVG + non-image types are rejected by signature check.

2	import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
3	import { realUser } from "./auth";

5	/**
6	 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
7	 *
8	 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
9	 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
10	 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
11	 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
12	 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
13	 */
14	export type Area =
15	  | "overview"
16	  | "analytics"
17	  | "clients"
18	  | "support"
19	  | "fleet"
20	  | "billing"
21	  | "platform";
22	
23	/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
24	export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
25	  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
26	  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
27	  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
28	  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
29	  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
30	  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
31	  platform: ["ADMIN"],
32	};
33	
34	export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
35	  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
36	}
37	
38	/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
39	export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
40	  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
41	}

43	/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
44	const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {

87	  return HREF_AREA[href] ?? "platform";

91	  return canAccess(role, areaForHref(href));

94	/**
95	 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
96	 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
97	 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
98	 */
99	export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
100	  const user = await realUser();
101	  if (!user) redirect("/login");
102	  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
103	  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
104	  return user;
105	}

### Security controls enforced (all server-side, client checks are UX-only)
1. **MIME allow-list**: only `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`. Everything else rejected.
2. **SVG explicitly rejected** — both by declared-type check (`image/svg+xml` → "SVG images are not allowed") and because SVG has no binary signature so `sniffImageMime` returns null.
3. **Real-bytes signature validation** — PNG `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`, JPEG `FF D8 FF`, GIF `47 49 46 38`, WEBP `RIFF....WEBP`. Stored MIME is the *sniffed* one; a declared/sniffed mismatch is rejected. A renamed/lying file (SVG or HTML claiming `image/png`) is rejected.
4. **5 MB cap** — cheap `file.size` guard before buffering, plus authoritative length check in `validateImageBytes`.
5. **Authorization** mirrors existing chat auth exactly — upload: visitor scoped by `visitorId` (or staff via `requireArea("support")`); serve: staff (`isStaff`), OR matching `visitorId`, OR the linked signed-in `userId`. Unauthorized viewers get 403.
6. **Rate-limited** via `checkRateLimit` — 15/min per IP (customer), 30/min per staff id.
7. **Serving headers**: `Content-Type` from stored mime, `Content-Disposition: inline; filename="image"`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox`. Never served as HTML; `id` is a DB id so no path traversal.
